::: {.callout-note}
## Learning objectives

- Write a rule with `input:`, `output:` and `shell:`.
- Ask for a target on the command line, and read a dry run (`-n`, `-p`).
- Predict when Snakemake reruns a job because a file changed.
- Match a rule's `output:` to the files a tool really writes.

Time: 40 min
:::

## Where you work

Make a folder two levels below the course root, so the course data are at
`../../data` (the stopping points use the same layout):

```bash
cd snakemake-course
mkdir -p work/regpipe
cd work/regpipe
```

Everything in this module goes into one file, `work/regpipe/Snakefile`.
Snakemake looks for a file with that name in the folder you run it from.

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
Keep the course environment active (`conda activate snakemake-course`) in the
terminal you use. All the tools in this module, `bowtie2`, `samtools` and
`fastqc`, come from it.
:::

## A first rule

The bowtie2 index is the step every alignment waits for. As a rule:

```{.python filename="Snakefile"}
rule bowtie2_index:
    input:
        "../../data/reference/chr8_course.fa.gz",
    output:
        multiext("output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome",
                 ".1.bt2", ".2.bt2", ".3.bt2", ".4.bt2", ".rev.1.bt2", ".rev.2.bt2"),
    shell:
        "bowtie2-build {input} output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome"
```

- `input:` the files the step reads. They must exist, or another rule must
  make them.
- `output:` the files the step writes. `bowtie2-build` writes six files that
  share one prefix; `multiext()` lists them without typing the prefix six
  times.
- `shell:` the command. `{input}` is replaced by the input path when the job
  runs.

::: {.notes}
Point out that the rule is a recipe. Writing it runs nothing. Nothing happens
until something asks for one of its outputs.
:::

## Dry run first

Before running anything, ask Snakemake what it would do:

```bash
snakemake -n -p
```

`-n` (`--dry-run`) plans the jobs and runs none of them. `-p` prints each shell
command with the paths filled in.

<!-- GENERATE: lesson01-dryrun | stopping-points/stopA | cat > Snakefile <<'EOF'
rule bowtie2_index:
    input:
        "../../data/reference/chr8_course.fa.gz",
    output:
        multiext("output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome",
                 ".1.bt2", ".2.bt2", ".3.bt2", ".4.bt2", ".rev.1.bt2", ".rev.2.bt2"),
    shell:
        "bowtie2-build {input} output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome"
EOF
snakemake -n -p -->

{{< generated name="lesson01-dryrun" command="false" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
Read it from the top. The job stats table counts jobs per rule (one here). Each
job then shows its input, output, and the `reason` it has to run: the outputs
are missing. The last lines repeat the counts. "This was a dry-run" at the end
means nothing ran.
:::

## Run it

```bash
snakemake --cores 4
```

`--cores` says how many CPU cores Snakemake may use at once. The index takes
a few seconds on the course reference (6.3 s on a 4-core laptop). Now run the
same command again:

```text
Building DAG of jobs...
Nothing to be done (all requested files are present and up to date).
```

The outputs exist and are newer than the input, so there is nothing to do.
That is the first idea in Snakemake: a job runs because its output is missing
or out of date, never just because it is in the file.

## A second rule: align one sample

Add this below the index rule. It aligns one sample, written out in full:

```{.python filename="Snakefile"}
rule align:
    input:
        fastq = "../../data/fastq/HCT116_CTCF_1.fastq.gz",
        index = rules.bowtie2_index.output,
    output:
        bam = "output/HCT116_CTCF_1/HCT116_CTCF_1_aligned.bam",
    shell:
        """
        bowtie2 -x output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome -U {input.fastq} \
            | samtools sort -o {output.bam} -
        """
```

- Inputs and outputs can have names. `{input.fastq}` is one file;
  `{input}` alone would be all of them, separated by spaces.
- `rules.bowtie2_index.output` is the output list of the other rule. The
  index files are inputs of `align`, so Snakemake knows `align` has to wait
  for `bowtie2_index`.
- A triple-quoted string holds a multi-line command. Snakemake runs it with
  bash in strict mode (`set -euo pipefail`), so if `bowtie2` fails in the
  middle of the pipe, the job fails.

## Targets on the command line

Run `snakemake -n` now and it still plans nothing. With no target, Snakemake
makes the outputs of the **first rule in the file**, and those exist. Name
what you want instead, either a file or a rule:

```bash
snakemake -n -p output/HCT116_CTCF_1/HCT116_CTCF_1_aligned.bam
snakemake -n -p align          # the same, by rule name
```

<!-- GENERATE: lesson01-dryrun-align | stopping-points/stopA | cat > Snakefile <<'EOF'
rule bowtie2_index:
    input:
        "../../data/reference/chr8_course.fa.gz",
    output:
        multiext("output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome",
                 ".1.bt2", ".2.bt2", ".3.bt2", ".4.bt2", ".rev.1.bt2", ".rev.2.bt2"),
    shell:
        "bowtie2-build {input} output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome"
rule align:
    input:
        fastq = "../../data/fastq/HCT116_CTCF_1.fastq.gz",
        index = rules.bowtie2_index.output,
    output:
        bam = "output/HCT116_CTCF_1/HCT116_CTCF_1_aligned.bam",
    shell:
        """
        bowtie2 -x output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome -U {input.fastq} \
            | samtools sort -o {output.bam} -
        """
EOF
snakemake --cores 4 bowtie2_index > /dev/null 2>&1
snakemake -n -p align -->

{{< generated name="lesson01-dryrun-align" command="false" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
The index is already built, so only `align` is planned. If you had deleted
`output/`, the same command would plan both jobs, index first. Asking by rule
name only works for a rule whose outputs are fixed names, like these two. In
module 2 rules get wildcards, and then you ask for files.
:::

Run it for real with `snakemake --cores 4 align`.

## How Snakemake decides a file is out of date

The basic rule is about modification times. A job reruns when one of its
inputs is newer than its outputs. Touch one index file and ask again:

```bash
touch output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome.1.bt2
snakemake -n align
```

<!-- GENERATE: lesson01-touch | stopping-points/stopA | cat > Snakefile <<'EOF'
rule bowtie2_index:
    input:
        "../../data/reference/chr8_course.fa.gz",
    output:
        multiext("output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome",
                 ".1.bt2", ".2.bt2", ".3.bt2", ".4.bt2", ".rev.1.bt2", ".rev.2.bt2"),
    shell:
        "bowtie2-build {input} output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome"
rule align:
    input:
        fastq = "../../data/fastq/HCT116_CTCF_1.fastq.gz",
        index = rules.bowtie2_index.output,
    output:
        bam = "output/HCT116_CTCF_1/HCT116_CTCF_1_aligned.bam",
    shell:
        """
        bowtie2 -x output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome -U {input.fastq} \
            | samtools sort -o {output.bam} -
        """
EOF
snakemake --cores 4 align > /dev/null 2>&1
touch output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome.1.bt2
snakemake -n align -->

{{< generated name="lesson01-touch" command="false" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
The reason line names the file: `Updated input files`. The index itself is
not rebuilt, because its own input (the FASTA) is older than it.

Timestamps are not the only trigger. Snakemake 8 also reruns a job when the
rule's code, its `params`, its list of input files or its software
environment changed since the output was made. It keeps those records in the
hidden `.snakemake/` folder. Module 4 shows the `params` case and how to
switch the extra triggers off.
:::

::: {.notes}
Real use: someone rebuilds the index "just to be safe" and every alignment
reruns. Module 4 shows `protected()` for exactly this.
:::

## A third rule: FastQC

```{.python filename="Snakefile"}
rule fastqc:
    input:
        "../../data/fastq/HCT116_CTCF_1.fastq.gz",
    output:
        html = "output/HCT116_CTCF_1/fastqc/HCT116_CTCF_1_fastqc.html",
        zip = "output/HCT116_CTCF_1/fastqc/HCT116_CTCF_1_fastqc.zip",
    shell:
        "fastqc --outdir output/HCT116_CTCF_1/fastqc {input}"
```

FastQC chooses its own file names: it takes the FASTQ name, drops
`.fastq.gz` and adds `_fastqc.html` and `_fastqc.zip`. The `output:` has to
say exactly those names. Snakemake does not tell the tool where to write;
it checks afterwards that the files you promised are there.

```bash
snakemake -n fastqc
snakemake --cores 4 fastqc
```

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
Snakemake creates the folder of each output before the job starts, so
`output/HCT116_CTCF_1/fastqc/` exists when FastQC writes into it. You do not
need `mkdir -p` for the parents of declared files.
:::

## What you have

```text
work/regpipe/
├── Snakefile                 # bowtie2_index, align, fastqc
└── output/
    ├── reference/bowtie2_index/genome.{1,2,3,4,rev.1,rev.2}.bt2
    └── HCT116_CTCF_1/
        ├── HCT116_CTCF_1_aligned.bam
        └── fastqc/HCT116_CTCF_1_fastqc.{html,zip}
```

Every path for `HCT116_CTCF_1` is typed out. Ten samples would mean ten copies
of `align`. Module 2 fixes that with wildcards.

## Exercise 1.2: What reruns?

All three rules have run and everything is up to date. For each change,
predict which jobs `snakemake -n align fastqc` plans, then check:

1. `touch output/HCT116_CTCF_1/HCT116_CTCF_1_aligned.bam`
2. `touch ../../data/fastq/HCT116_CTCF_1.fastq.gz` (only in your own copy of
   the data, or think it through)
3. You delete `output/reference/` and run `snakemake -n` with no target.

## Exercise 1.3: Spot the error

A labmate's FastQC rule dry-runs without complaint but fails every time it
runs, even though FastQC itself finishes. Why?

```{.python filename="Snakefile"}
rule fastqc:
    input:
        "../../data/fastq/HCT116_CTCF_1.fastq.gz",
    output:
        html = "output/HCT116_CTCF_1/fastqc/HCT116_CTCF_1.html",
        zip = "output/HCT116_CTCF_1/fastqc/HCT116_CTCF_1.zip",
    shell:
        "fastqc --outdir output/HCT116_CTCF_1/fastqc {input}"
```

What error do you expect, and what is the smallest fix?

[Answer](../answers/01-rules-answers.qmd#ex-1.3)
:::

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}

Move `rule fastqc` to the top of the Snakefile and run `snakemake -n` in a
fresh folder (no `output/`). What is planned now, and why did it change?

## Key points

- A rule says which files it reads (`input:`), which it writes (`output:`)
  and how (`shell:`). It runs only when something needs its outputs.
- With no target, Snakemake makes the first rule's outputs. Otherwise name a
  file or a rule on the command line.
- Always dry-run first: `snakemake -n -p` shows the jobs, the reason for each
  and the exact commands.
- A job reruns when an input is newer than its outputs (and, in Snakemake 8,
  when its code, params or software changed).
- `output:` must match what the tool writes, name for name.
